newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OMV sees higher 1997 crude, gas production.
newsitem.headline: OMV sees higher 1997 crude, gas production.

text.p: Austria's OMV said on Tuesday it aimed to boost 1997 crude oil production by 30 percent to 2.5 million tonnes and increase gas production by 19 percent to one billion cubic metres.
Chief Executive Richard Schenz told a press conference new production coming on-stream in Libya, the North Sea and Austria would more than offset declining output at old Austrian wells.
"Overall in Austria there will be a slight decline in crude production this year but then one has to add in the new fields abroad," Schenz said.
In 1996 Austrian crude oil production eased to 1.92 million tonnes from 1.93 million the previous year. Gas production stood at 0.84 billion cubic metres.
Schenz said the gas production figure would rise this year following the start-up of a desulphurisation plant.
The firm planned to invest roughly 1.5 billion schillings in E&P this year, compared with 1.8 billion in 1996.
Operations in Albania, where the firm is seeking an onshore concession, were returning to normal despite unrest in the country.
"Our office is open and our key staff are there," Schenz said.
